entries.title: Validate the artifact and its target environment together
entries.trigger: a release depends on database, RPC, function, runtime configuration or native changes.
entries.mechanism: the source suite passes against local changes while the distributed client calls an undeployed dependency, or an OTA reaches a binary with an incompatible native runtime.
entries.prevention: map client callers to hosted dependencies, verify deployment inventory, and identify the exact artifact/runtime before release. Keep migration rollout order and rollback explicit. Check each platform's runtime compatibility; one platform's success does not establish the other's. Treat dispatch, finished artifact, upload, store processing, distribution, and physical acceptance as separate gates. Preserve explicit authorization and notification intent when dispatching or monitoring work.
verification: inspect required hosted versions and the built artifact, then run the real installed flow. For durable-state changes include fresh install, new account, sign-out, retained-account sign-in, restore and opening restricted/shared media. A published manifest is not a device launch. Verify every prerequisite named by an assertion: a job acknowledgement with an authenticated user still present cannot prove post-deletion receipt survival, and a sequential pending-state fixture is not concurrent transaction evidence.
boundaries: 2026-09-06, Expo SDK 57 / EAS Update. Runtime policies and native dependencies must be re-evaluated after changes; do not carry a prior fingerprint forward by assumption.

entries.title: Migration IDs do not prove executable schema parity
entries.trigger: a local or hosted database is reused while migration files are developed or amended.
entries.mechanism: the migration ledger records an applied version, but its functions can still contain an earlier definition. Tests pass against that stale database instead of the current source.
entries.prevention: before accepting a migration baseline, rebuild a named disposable database from current files. Compare actual owned definitions and permissions with the target environment when parity matters. Never rewrite a deployed migration or stamp ledger versions to conceal a difference.
verification: run the complete relevant database suite on the clean database, then classify every definition/grant difference. Preserve environment-specific and extension exclusions explicitly. A hash comparison of functions alone does not establish table, policy, configuration, or data parity.

verify every secondary test connection too. A dblink fixture using a fixed host port can commit into another local project while assertions read the isolated database. Use the selected server endpoint and preserve its authentication requirements; localhost trust can make ordinary dblink reject a non-superuser even when a password is supplied. Confirm exact cleanup in the actual target.
boundaries: 2026-09-07, PostgreSQL 17.6 and Supabase CLI 2.114.0 isolated db start. Re-evaluate tooling after upgrades; the distinction between a migration identifier and its applied contents is general.

entries.title: Runtime validation cannot protect already inlined build variables
entries.trigger: a bundler replaces public environment references in client JavaScript.
entries.mechanism: a runtime rejection happens after a privileged value has entered the artifact; an externally changed export environment can also reuse a cached previous literal.
entries.prevention: reject forbidden value classes during build configuration without echoing their values. Never put a private credential in public variables. Use supported cache clearing when switching external export inputs and inspect the emitted artifact using synthetic markers during validation.
verification: invalid synthetic input fails before output; valid input produces only the expected literal in each platform bundle after cache clearing. Old artifacts remain separate incident scope.
boundaries: 2026-09-07, Expo SDK 57/Metro; export --clear and EAS Update --clear-cache. Recheck CLI flags and environment cache behavior on upgrade; do not assume every ordinary dotenv edit needs clearing.
